newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force reports crew error in Honduras crash.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force reports crew error in Honduras crash.

text.p: The United States Air Force said on Friday crew error was one of the main reasons a C-130 Hercules plane crashed on landing in Honduras in April, killing three people.
The Accident Investigation Board found no evidence of aircraft or flight systems malfunctions, the Air Force said in a statement.
The board found that the crew failed to "accurately assess and understand" landing requirements at Toncontin International Airport in Tegucigalpa, Honduras.
"The board also stated that the crew maintained a higher than computed approach airspeed and landed the aircraft too far down the runway to stop in time," the statement said.
Three members of the 440th Airlift Wing from the General Mitchell Air Reserve Station in Wisconsin died in the crash. There were seven survivors.

According to the report, the C-130 went off the runway, hit a concrete drainage ditch, went through a fence over a sheer 50-foot (15 metre) drop-off and finally stopped on a civilian highway interchange where it caught fire.
